title: Cold rebuild: Read docker ps
summary: Rebuild Read docker ps from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Read docker ps** in *run, ps, logs, exec*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: The `api` container crashed and shows `Exited (1)`. You run `docker exec -it api sh`. What happens?
options: An error: the container is not running, so there is no process to join
A shell opens inside the stopped container
Docker restarts the container and opens a shell
A shell opens in a fresh container from the same image
steps.explain: `exec` needs a running container. Start with `docker logs api` to see why it exited.

steps.title: Rebuild Read docker ps cold
prompt: A script ran `docker ps -a --format "{{.Names}}|{{.Image}}|{{.Status}}|{{.Ports}}"`. Write `List<string> Summarize(List<string> lines)` that turns each line into a short summary:
| `Up` | `NAME: running` or, when Ports is not empty, `NAME: running (PORTS)` |
| anything else | `NAME: ` + the first word of Status in lower case (`Created` → `created`) |
